source.author: verg
source.text: hinc exaudiri voces et verba vocantis visa viri, nox cum terras obscura teneret; solaque culminibus ferali carmine bubo saepe queri et longas in fletum ducere voces; multaque praeterea vatum praedicta priorum terribili monitu horrificant.
source.text_original: hinc exaudiri voces et verba vocantis / visa viri, nox cum terras obscura teneret; / solaque culminibus ferali carmine bubo / saepe queri et longas in fletum ducere voces; / multaque praeterea vatum praedicta priorum / terribili monitu horrificant.
source.text_english: From here voices and the words of a man calling were thought to be heard, when dark night held the lands; and on the roofs the lone screech-owl was often heard lamenting in a funereal cry and drawing out long calls into weeping; and many other predictions of seers of old, with fearful warning, made men tremble.

reuse.author: val
reuse.text: sed non ulla quies animo fratrisque paventi progeniem divumque minas; hunc nam fore regi exitio vatesque canunt pecudumque per aras terrifici monitus iterant: super ipsius ingens instat fama viri virtusque haut laeta tyranno.
reuse.text_original: sed non ulla quies animo fratrisque paventi / progeniem divumque minas; hunc nam fore regi / exitio vatesque canunt pecudumque per aras / terrifici monitus iterant: super ipsius ingens / instat fama viri virtusque haut laeta tyranno.
reuse.text_english: but there was no rest for his mind, nor for his fearful brother, because of the offspring and the threats of the gods; for seers proclaim that this man will be the king’s destruction, and the dreadful warnings repeat themselves through the altars of the sacrificial beasts: over and above the man himself looms a great renown and a valor not pleasing to the tyrant.
